the fire impact on hydrological regime of the Rimbaud basin is negligible.
fire has a minor impact on the hydrological response of the Rimbaud catchment, which is in line with the results of other studies on fire impacts on the Mediterranean watersheds.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

fire impact can be detected in the hydrological response of the watershed only if the analysis is focused at the right time scale and if the modelling approach is based on the right set of model parameters.
the fire has not caused a significant change in the hydrological regime of the Rimbaud catchment.
the impact of fire on the hydrology of the Mediterranean catchment is not as dramatic as it was thought.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it is possible to detect the impact of fire on hydrological response of small catchments by data analysis and modelling.
the fire impact on hydrology can be detected only by detailed analysis of hydrographs, while the use of lumped parameters models can lead to misleading conclusions.
a simple model with few parameters can satisfactorily represent the hydrological response of small Mediterranean watersheds to fire.
